summary: One conditional high, ten medium, four low, and one informational source-review finding were triaged. All fourteen actionable items are remediated. Stateless SAML single-consumption and application-owned IdP group authorization remain documented architecture decisions.

findings.disposition: Make the backend-installed distribution and exact backend wheel authoritative; verify a server-owned complete-wheel SHA-256 before browser installation and make public-index use explicit.
findings.implementation: Hosted runtime installation now probes the declared-version and development-version backend wheels before any index source, installs the backend URL only with its X-Pytincture-SHA256 complete-wheel lock, retains the built-in dhxpyt immutable wheel lock, and allows a custom PyPI fallback only when the exact canonical spec appears in PYTINCTURE_WIDGET_PUBLIC_INDEX_ALLOWLIST.
regression_tests: pytincture/frontend/tests/lifecycle.test.mjs: backend wheel wins before a matching public-index package
pytincture/frontend/tests/lifecycle.test.mjs: service custom widgets fail closed instead of silently using PyPI
pytincture/frontend/tests/lifecycle.test.mjs: an exact service widget may use PyPI only after explicit allowlisting
findings.compatibility_note: Custom widgetsets remain supported and continue to be installed on the backend. Private widgets no longer yield priority to an equal public package name and version.

findings.disposition: Preserve stateless SAML browser transactions. Add accurate fresh-client replay coverage and offer a vendor-neutral atomic provider only as an optional strict mode.
findings.existing_mitigation: Signed browser binding, short transaction and assertion expiry, ACS rate limiting, normal-browser replay rejection, secure cookies, and session audience controls.
findings.compatibility_note: No Redis, process memory, sticky routing, or shared store is required. Global single consumption is impossible without shared atomic state.

findings.disposition: Bound capped request-body ingress before BFF execution admission with a separate configurable timeout.
findings.implementation: The BFF dependency reads and progressively byte-limits the body under BFF_REQUEST_INGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS before acquiring BFF_ADMISSION_GATE. The execution deadline starts only after admission.
findings.compatibility_note: Only slow request upload is bounded; long-running backend execution retains its separate timeout.

findings.disposition: Bound each blocked streaming response write and release stream admission exactly once after timeout.
findings.implementation: Every ASGI stream frame is sent under the independent BFF_STREAM_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS deadline. Timeout completes admission once and closes the bounded iterator; each successfully moving frame receives a fresh deadline.
findings.compatibility_note: Generators, async generators, yield, moving chunks, and long-running streams remain supported; only a blocked client write is disconnected.

findings.disposition: Bound OAuth initiation and callback rates, exchange concurrency, and provider deadlines; validate application existence before initiation.
findings.implementation: OAuth initiation and callback routes now apply configurable per-peer/application/provider rate controls. Token exchange uses a bounded per-worker admission gate, explicit HTTP phase deadlines, and an overall deadline. Application existence is verified with contained no-follow file metadata before any provider work.
findings.compatibility_note: Normal OAuth remains stateless, load-balancer friendly, and Redis-free. Limits are deliberately generous and configurable. Strict globally atomic callback consumption remains optional.

findings.disposition: Preserve signed IdP group values as authenticated identity claims. Application code, decorators, and policies own authorization and any mapping.
findings.existing_mitigation: An attacker cannot forge signed group values; Pytincture defines no implicit privileged group name.
findings.compatibility_note: SAML_ALLOWED_ROLES is login eligibility, not a filter or framework-owned grant mapping.

findings.disposition: Enforce finite expiration, not-before, issued-at, clock-skew, maximum-age, and maximum-lifetime policy for MCP JWTs.
findings.implementation: The Pytincture JWT verifier now requires finite exp and iat claims by default, enforces optional nbf, rejects future or over-age tokens, and caps exp-to-iat lifetime. Clock skew, age, and lifetime are typed settings. A disabled-by-default legacy flag permits migration from timeless tokens.
findings.compatibility_note: Non-expiring tokens require migration or the explicit MCP_ALLOW_LEGACY_TIMELESS_TOKENS compatibility setting. Normal expiring tokens, MCP scopes, and BFF mappings are unchanged.

findings.disposition: Use host-prefixed HTTPS production authentication cookies and separate unprefixed HTTP development cookie names.
findings.implementation: HTTPS production uses __Host-pytincture-session and __Host-pytincture-csrf plus an application-specific __Host-pytincture-saml-handshake-* cookie. Every host-prefixed cookie is Secure, has Path=/, and has no Domain attribute. Local HTTP development uses separate pytincture-dev-* names, and generated/browser BFF clients recognize both CSRF names.
findings.compatibility_note: Production users need one fresh login because legacy cookie names are deliberately ignored. Local HTTP development remains supported. Application-specific SAML cookie names preserve concurrent handshakes for different applications.

findings.disposition: Cache bounded per-application graph snapshots with secure automatic invalidation and early impossible-operation rejection.
findings.implementation: BFF dispatch rejects missing registry operations before graph discovery. Valid targets use a bounded per-worker LRU keyed by application, browser-file declarations, root, and limits. Warm hits securely stat selected source identities and relevant directories; source edits, additions, removals, or newly glob-matched files invalidate before reuse. Cold discovery applies APPCODE file, per-file byte, and aggregate byte limits plus explicit directory and scanned-file bounds.
findings.compatibility_note: The process-local cache remains stateless and disposable. Same-name development edits and new matching files invalidate automatically. The default bounds are generous and configurable; no Redis, sticky routing, or shared state is introduced.

findings.disposition: Cache public-asset authorization and add configurable admission, byte, and blocked-write limits.
findings.implementation: A bounded per-worker cache reuses parsed authorization only while the secure application entrypoint and relevant directories remain unchanged. Generous configurable worker admission plus per-peer concurrency and rate controls run before source parsing or file opening. Direct assets have configurable byte, total-duration, and per-frame blocked-write limits with idempotent descriptor and admission cleanup.
findings.compatibility_note: Public assets remain unauthenticated. The 64 MiB default can be raised for large media. Moving responses reset the write deadline; same-name source and asset changes remain visible. All state is disposable and worker-local, so Redis and sticky routing are unnecessary.

findings.disposition: Make replay-refill quota accounting denial-safe through ordered short-circuiting or transactional reservations.
findings.implementation: Replay refill now checks the ordered session, peer, and worker buckets under one atomic multi-limiter admission operation. Counts are committed only when every bucket permits the refill; any denial leaves every bucket unchanged.
findings.compatibility_note: Accepted requests, configured limits, stateless operation, and valid-user throughput are unchanged. Replay refill remains disabled by default and requires neither Redis nor sticky routing.

findings.disposition: Key only isolated-process fairness to an HMAC-protected stable authenticated identity and retain configurable concurrency with bounded admission.
findings.implementation: The optional isolated-process executor now keys its per-identity active-call counter to a domain-separated HMAC over provider, issuer, tenant, and immutable subject. Built-in local authentication falls back to normalized email only when no subject exists. External identities without a subject share a conservative provider bucket instead of using mutable email or a refreshable session ID. Anonymous isolated calls use an HMAC-protected peer bucket.
findings.compatibility_note: Multiple sessions for one authenticated identity share only the existing configurable isolated-process concurrency allowance. This is not a request-volume quota. Ordinary cooperative async/sync BFF calls, normal async multitasking, and streaming are unaffected; no shared storage, Redis, or sticky routing is required.

findings.disposition: Expose immutable Microsoft identity clearly, document it for sensitive authorization, and warn when production admission relies only on mutable email.
findings.implementation: Microsoft callbacks retain the tenant-scoped immutable Entra object id as oid in the signed browser identity. Stateless application admission accepts object_ids alongside tenant/issuer/subject/role constraints. Startup emits a structured security.microsoft_mutable_email_admission warning when global or per-application Microsoft admission relies only on mutable email or domain.
findings.compatibility_note: Email and domain admission remain available for simple applications. The new warning is advisory, object_ids is additive, signed sessions remain browser-carried, and no Redis or sticky routing is introduced.

findings.disposition: Equalize oversized-password failure work and transparently migrate successful bcrypt verification to Argon2id when supported.
findings.implementation: Known bcrypt passwords exceeding 72 UTF-8 bytes are denied through the same Argon2id dummy verification used for an unknown account, eliminating bcrypt 5's fast ValueError oracle. The credential-store helper returns a current Argon2id replacement after successful bcrypt verification or when an Argon2id hash needs rehashing.
findings.compatibility_note: Password values and the login API do not change. Static AUTH_PASSWORD_HASHES remains immutable and stateless; custom authenticators with mutable external stores may persist the optional replacement without Redis or process-local state.

findings.disposition: Compare exact runtime type and value for Literal validation and handle None explicitly.
findings.implementation: Static BFF Literal validation requires exact runtime type plus equal value for every option and handles None only through identity. Python's bool/int/float equality aliases cannot cross the JSON request boundary.
findings.compatibility_note: Only JSON values whose type violates the declared annotation are rejected. Correctly typed bool, int, float, string, and None literals remain accepted.

findings.disposition: Retain existing public/authenticated/disabled API-documentation modes and add public/minimal/operator detail modes to the always-public health and readiness status probes.
findings.implementation: Health and readiness always expose their status and meaningful HTTP code. PYTINCTURE_DIAGNOSTIC_DETAILS_MODE=minimal omits version and named checks; operator mode returns details only for a constant-time matched strong Bearer token. Responses are private/no-store, operator responses vary on Authorization, and all controls are stateless.
findings.compatibility_note: The default response bodies remain unchanged. Minimal and operator modes are opt-in, load balancer status stays public, and no Redis or sticky routing is required.

accepted_residual_risks.reason: Immediate fleet-wide revocation of a copied stateless cookie requires shared mutable state. Absolute expiry, key rotation, Secure and HttpOnly cookies, and application audience restrictions remain the no-store controls.
Hosted service mode uses the vendored runtime. External runtime mode is an explicit application trust decision and its bootstrap scripts retain SRI.
A policy hook returning None retains the documented allow compatibility contract; application-owned conditional policies must explicitly deny or raise.
Python threads cannot be killed safely. Isolated-process mode provides bounded killable containment for trusted non-streaming work that requires hard termination.
Pytincture authenticates selected browser packages but does not sandbox separately maintained widgetset implementations.
